ing: carp, sea bass or trout, cleaned and butterflied
st: Ask the fish seller to cut the fish open along the belly or back so it lies flat like a book, and remove the guts. Rinse and pat dry.
Mix the lemon juice, turmeric, oil, salt, pepper, garlic and tamarind into a paste.
Rub the paste all over the fish and inside the cavity. Marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Heat a grill or the oven broiler to medium-high. For the oven, heat to 425°F (220°C) and place a rack in the middle.
Lay the fish skin side down on an oiled grill grate or baking sheet. Top the flesh with the tomato slices and onion rings.
Cook for 25 to 30 minutes without flipping, until the flesh is opaque and flakes easily and reads 145°F (63°C) in the thickest part.
Let the fish rest for 5 minutes, then lift onto a platter.
Serve with the grilled tomato and onion, lemon wedges, flatbread and a plain salad.
Soak the grape leaves in hot water for 10 minutes to remove the brine. Rinse and trim any thick stems.
Mix the rice, lamb, onion, diced tomato, garlic, parsley, tomato paste, cinnamon, salt and pepper in a bowl. Add [[2 tbsp]] of the oil.
Line the bottom of a heavy pot with a few torn leaves and the tomato slices to prevent burning.
Lay a leaf shiny side down. Put about [[1 tbsp]] filling near the stem end, fold in the sides, and roll up snugly but not tight, as the rice will swell.
Pack the rolls seam side down in tight circles in the pot.
Pour the hot broth, lemon juice and the remaining [[1 tbsp]] oil over the top. Set a plate on top to hold the rolls down.
Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low for 50 minutes until the rice is tender and the lamb reaches 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 10 minutes off the heat, then serve warm with yogurt.

ing: for the dough, plus more to boil
st: Boil the rice with the water and [[1 tsp]] salt in a covered pot for 20 minutes until very soft and sticky.
While it cooks, heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pan. Cook half the onions for 5 minutes, then add the beef and cook for 8 minutes until browned and fully cooked.
Stir in the allspice, cinnamon, pepper, [[1 tsp]] salt, parsley, raisins and almonds. Cool completely.
Mash the hot rice with the remaining onion and the turmeric until a smooth dough forms. Cool until you can handle it.
Wet your hands. Take a ball of dough the size of an egg and press a hollow in it with your thumb to make a cup.
Fill with [[1 tbsp]] of the beef mixture, pinch the edges closed, and smooth into an oval. Chill the shaped kubba for 20 minutes.
Heat 2 inches of oil to 350°F (175°C) in a deep pan.
Fry the kubba in batches for 4 to 5 minutes until deep golden and crisp, then drain and serve hot.
Heat the oven to 325°F (160°C). Rub the lamb with salt, pepper, cumin, allspice, cardamom and garlic.
Melt [[1 tbsp]] butter in a Dutch oven and brown the lamb on all sides for 10 minutes. Remove it.
Cook the onions in the same pot for 6 minutes. Add the cinnamon stick and [[1.5 cup]] of the hot broth.
Return the lamb, cover tightly, and roast for 2.5 hours until very tender and falling off the bone.
Lift the lamb out and keep it warm. Strain the cooking liquid and add enough broth to measure [[3 cup]].
Stir the rice into the liquid in a pot, bring to a boil, then cover and cook on low for 15 minutes. Rest for 10 minutes.
Fry the almonds and raisins in [[2 tbsp]] butter for 2 minutes until golden and puffed.
Pile the rice on a platter, set the lamb on top, and scatter the nuts and raisins over everything.

ing: pierced with a fork, or use 2 tbsp lemon juice
torn into pieces, such as pita or samoon
st: Heat the oil in a large pot and brown the lamb for 8 minutes. Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the turmeric, cumin, salt and cinnamon stick for 1 minute.
Add the water, tomatoes and dried limes. Bring to a boil, skim the foam, then cover.
Simmer on low for 1.5 hours until the lamb is tender.
Add the chickpeas and simmer for 15 minutes more. Remove the cinnamon.
Toast the torn bread in a low oven or dry pan until crisp, and divide among deep bowls.
Ladle the hot broth, lamb and chickpeas over the bread. Let it soak for 2 minutes and serve.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Brush the eggplant slices with [[2 tbsp]] oil, sprinkle with [[0.5 tsp]] salt, and bake on trays for 20 minutes until soft and lightly brown.
Mix the beef, onion, garlic, parsley, allspice, pepper and [[1 tsp]] salt. Shape into small meatballs the size of walnuts.
Brown the meatballs in [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet for 6 minutes. They will finish cooking in the oven.
Whisk the tomato paste with the water and the remaining salt and oil.
In a deep baking dish, layer the potatoes first, then the eggplant, then the meatballs, then the tomato slices.
Pour the tomato mixture over the top. Cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 40 minutes, then remove the foil and bake for 10 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the meatballs read 160°F (71°C).
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with rice or bread.

ing: peeled, or use canned fava beans
st: Rinse the fava beans. Boil them with the water and turmeric for 40 minutes until soft.
Drain, keeping about a cup of the cooking liquid. Stir in the salt and pepper.
Melt [[2 tbsp]] butter in a pan and cook the onion for 5 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the beans and half the reserved liquid and warm through for 3 minutes.
Lay the torn bread in shallow bowls and spoon the beans and some broth over it.
Melt the remaining [[2 tbsp]] butter in a skillet and fry the eggs until the whites are set, about 3 minutes.
Top each bowl with an egg and sprinkle with the dill. Serve hot.
Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt in a large bowl.
Add the warm water and oil. Stir into a shaggy dough, then knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Heat the oven to 475°F (245°C) with a baking sheet or stone inside.
Divide the dough into 8 pieces and shape each into a ball. Let rest for 10 minutes.
Roll each ball into a diamond shape about 1/2 inch thick, with pointed ends. Sprinkle with nigella seeds if you like.
Let the shapes rise for 20 minutes under a cloth.
Bake on the hot sheet for 10 to 12 minutes until golden with a crisp crust. Cool slightly and serve warm.
Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes.
Mix the flour, salt and [[0.5 tsp]] cardamom. Rub in [[0.75 cup]] of the butter until crumbly.
Add the yeast milk and knead into a soft dough. Rest, covered, for 30 minutes.
Cook the dates with the remaining [[0.25 cup]] butter, cinnamon and [[0.5 tsp]] cardamom in a pan for 5 minutes, mashing until a thick paste. Stir in the walnuts and cool.
Heat the oven to 350°F (175°C) and line a baking sheet.
Divide the dough into 24 balls. Flatten each, put about [[1 tbsp]] filling in the center, and close it into a ball.
Press each ball flat into a round cookie and mark the top with a fork.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes until pale golden. Cool on a rack.
